Subject: Plasma Attacks
ErrataText: Plasma Weapon Attacks should be +2 Multiplier versus shields, not "Double Damage" as described here. This brings it in line with the description for Counter: Shields on P212.

Subject: Terran psionic Force Fields
ErrataText: Terran Sphere psionics using force fields circumvent the restriction on Psionic effects by having a gap in their force field's protection. This means that their force fields may be bypassed by aimed or area attacks that happen while they are using their powers. Normally this vulnerability only lasts for the Psionics turn, leaving them vulnerable to sustained attacks, but ongoing effects require the gap to remain open and exploitable.

Subject: Armor reduction duration
ErrataText: Armor Reduction from Coordinated Fire or from attacks with Counter: Armor persists until the end of the round, allowing subsequent players to take advantage of the target's weakened state.

Subject: Battle Strain: missile salvos
ErrataText: Battle strain can be spent on a 1 to 1 basis to increase the number of missiles in a salvo. This can not be used in conjunction with the Coordinated fire effect.

Subject: Battle Strain: Tags and extra actions
ErrataText: Using Battle Strain to Activate Tags or Perform Extra Actions with a unit does not fall under the single Battle Strain expenditure per round rule. Additional extra actions after the first cost increasing multiples of 3 Battle Strain (6, 9, etc...) as per the extra actions for AP rule.

Subject: Attached characters: skill switch
ErrataText: A character attached to a unit may use Tags and their personal AP to skill switch from the unit's target number on to their corresponding skill.

Subject: Missile attacks vs margin of defense
ErrataText: Missile attacks reduce their targets' total margin of defense by the number of attacking missiles in the salvo not -1 per salvo launched at the target. This reduction is not restricted to their bonus margin of defense from anti missile fire.

Subject: Software: required computer
ErrataText: Software no longer requires a computer rank by size. Instead, program size sets the computer grade it needs. Tiny, Small, and Medium programs need a Minor computer, carry 1 or 2 Tasks, and serve a single user. Large and Huge programs need a Moderate computer, carry multiple Tasks, and serve dozens of users at once. Colossal programs need a Major computer and serve hundreds of users at once. Computer rank no longer limits program size; it only caps Task target numbers. A Task runs at its own TN or the computer rank's maximum TN, whichever is lower. Replace every "Required Computer Rank" in program stat blocks with the matching Required Computer Grade.

The Ships of the Line design exercise starting on page 219 provides an example of these rules in action.

Subject: Attack: Melee
ErrataText: Melee attacks can never gain the Area attribute.

Subject: Attack: rail weapon power
NewValue: integrated/slaved: Power Slot + Ammunition; standalone: self-powered rounds
ErrataText: Rail (Kinetic Ranged) weapons integrated into an item (ship and vehicle weapons, and units slaved to a host such as suit-mounted or Weapon Link weapons) draw a Power Slot like any other Attack, in addition to their Ammunition. Standalone rail weapons (hand weapons such as gauss pistols and rifles) need no Power Supply: the power is built into the casing of each round, and this is already included in their Ammunition.

Subject: Attack: Hyperspace implementation
ErrataText: The Hyperspace implementation (the Shohan Dreadnought's hyper cannon, the only such attack in the game) includes Counter: Armor and Area: Small Sudden at no extra cost. Both are printed in the cannon's stat block so its effects can be read without looking up the implementation.

Subject: Attack: One-Time Use feed
ErrataText: An Attack on a One-Time Use item, such as a grenade, needs no feed (no Power Slot and no Ammunition): the item is its own charge.

Subject: Attack: 1x attacks
NewValue: any no-damage attack delivering an effect, half the base cost
ErrataText: A 1x attack does no damage; it delivers an effect (Tags, Counters, or missile interception) and costs half the Attack base (5 / 10 / 20). The Anti-Missile is one example; the Deployment Companion's Flashbang is another.

Subject: Area: size
NewValue: 20 BP per size step (Small 20, Medium 40, Large 60)
ErrataText: Area costs 20 BP for a Small area. Each size step larger costs another 20 BP: Medium 40, Large 60, Huge 80, Colossal 100.

Subject: Attack: contact charges
NewValue: hand-to-hand weapons only; contact charges pay full price
ErrataText: An emplaced charge or grenade whose Attack is marked Melee is delivered by contact. It does not get the Melee half price, which applies only to hand-to-hand weapons. (Decisive Action's breaching and demolition charges.)

Subject: Attack: Plasma Bleed
FieldName: Plasma Bleed above the free amount
NewValue: Costs the difference between full Bleed cost and the free Bleed
ErrataText: A Plasma Attack's free Bleed (half its Weapon Multiplier, at the grade matching the Attack's scale) can be increased. Additional Bleed damage costs the difference between the full Bleed cost and the free Bleed.

Subject: Attack: self-powered Plasma
NewValue: Plasma (2 Power Slots per mount); Plasma (self-powered) (special ammunition, built-in Moderate limitation)
ErrataText: Plasma has a self-powered implementation for hand weapons. Instead of drawing 2 Power Slots per mount, it needs special ammunition (an Ammunition Resource). That requirement is built into the implementation as a Moderate limitation: it takes one of the two Moderate limitation slots but refunds no Build Points. Plasma weapons built into or slaved to a host still draw 2 Power Slots per mount, with or without ammunition. Kinetic (rail) weapons split the same way (p210): Kinetic draws a Power Slot plus Ammunition, Kinetic (self-powered) uses Ammunition only.

Subject: Counter: Armor
OldValue: -2, or ignore armor on an aimed attack
NewValue: -1 unaimed; -2 aimed; -1 carries to other attacks
ErrataText: Counter Armor no longer can bypass non-partial armor on an aimed attack. Instead on an unaimed attack it will reduce armor by 1. Aimed attacks will grant an additional 1 armor reduction for the attack, bringing the aimed attack to -2 armor. However, the armor reduction contributed to other attacks remains at -1 armor.

ErrataText: Counter: Strain raises or lowers Psionic Strain by 5 per Counter (20 BP each). Regeneration: Strain restores Psionic Strain like other Regeneration implementations. A drug's Duration is bought as a Resource (1 Minor rank ≈ 10 combat rounds or 1 hour; 1 Moderate rank ≈ 1 day).

ErrataText: Reactionless drives should not expel Reaction Mass.

Subject: Drive: Fuel exemptions
NewValue: not needed when a Coil, Environmental, or Hyperspace Tap Power Supply runs it, or for a Biological Drive
ErrataText: A Drive needs no Fuel Resource when it can run from its item's own Power Supply and that supply burns no Fuel: a Coil (battery), Environmental, or Hyperspace Tap supply. A creature's legs, wings, or fins are a Biological Drive, which needs no Fuel either. Light Sail and Jump drives are unchanged.

Subject: Hangar: capacity
ErrataText: Hangar: "multiple items" means 3 items, or 4 if crammed in. For example, a Major Hangar on a Huge ship holds 3 Large craft (4 crammed), and a Moderate Hangar holds 3 items two sizes smaller (4 crammed).

Subject: Launcher: sets of 4
ErrataText: Launchers are bought in sets of 4 (one set draws 1 Power Slot and costs 4 × the per-launcher price: 20 / 40 / 60 BP). Ships printing launcher counts that are not multiples of 4 are corrected by errata (Standard Assault Shuttle, Dragon, Conventional Frigate, Redemption, Havenite Marauder). A Magazine does not have to match the launcher count.

Subject: Regeneration: power
NewValue: Force Field and Mechanical: 1 slot each; Biological: none
ErrataText: Force Field Regeneration and Mechanical Regeneration each use 1 Power Slot, of the same grade as the item's Force Field (or its Attacks' scale if it has none). Biological Regeneration uses no Power Slot. (A Force Field itself uses 1 slot, as written on p214.)

Subject: Link: Refueling
ErrataText: Add a Link type, Refueling: a docking connection that transfers fuel to a linked craft of up to the Link's maximum size. Each Refueling Link draws 1 Power Slot of its grade while in use. (The Fleet Auxiliary's three Major Refueling Links account for 3 of its 4 used Power Slots.)

Subject: Link: Weapon power
NewValue: 1 Power Slot of its grade per Link (by default)
ErrataText: A Weapon Link powers the weapon it carries, so by default each Weapon Link uses 1 Power Slot of its grade. Some weapons need none, such as self-powered Kinetic (rail) weapons.

Subject: Link: Armor
ErrataText: Add a Link type, Armor: it holds a separately built armor kit up to the Link's maximum size. The kit's Armor Rating applies by default; an aimed shot can target the host's own Armor Rating instead. An Armor Link uses no Power Slot. (First used by the New Detroit militia's Ranger Armor and its Armor Kit.)

Subject: Link: Weapon (self-powered weapons)
NewValue: none when the carried weapon has its own Power Supply
ErrataText: A Weapon Link carrying a weapon that has its own Power Supply (such as a Shohan Tse Blade or Flare Pistol) uses no Power Slot, the same as a self-powered Kinetic weapon.

Subject: Power Supply: minimum item size
ErrataText: A Moderate Power Supply may be installed on a Small item (the table lists Medium). Major Power Supplies still require a Large item, except that the compact Hyperspace Tap and Coil implementations can squeeze a Major Power Supply into a Medium item.

Subject: Power Supply: minimum item size
FieldName: Minimum size: Major (Hyperspace Tap or Coil)
ErrataText: A Moderate Power Supply may be installed on a Small item (the table lists Medium). Major Power Supplies still require a Large item, except that the compact Hyperspace Tap and Coil implementations can squeeze a Major Power Supply into a Medium item.

Subject: Power: host-powered items
NewValue: draw their slots from the host
ErrataText: An item with no Power Supply or Drive of its own, such as a weapon module or a G3P, draws the Power Slots it uses from the host it is mounted on or plugged into. Its stat block lists them as its power requirement. A Slave limitation still means it needs a Link of the right type to work, not just a power connection.

Subject: Missiles: Space-scale chassis

ErrataText: A Space-scale missile is built on a chassis of a Moderate Reaction Drive and a Major Coil Power Supply, with no Charge or Fuel (it only has to last one round). Missile stat blocks assume the chassis and don't print it.

Subject: Resource: Fuel grade

ErrataText: A Fuel Resource can feed Drives and Power Supplies of its own grade or lower. A larger fuel tank can feed a smaller drive (for example, Major Fuel can feed a Moderate Reaction Drive), but never the reverse.
